ukmt-jk-2015-01.title: Count legs by group
ukmt-jk-2015-01.body:
Two-legged: Ben, father, mother, sister, brother (5 people) and 4 parrots, so $9\times 2=18$ legs. Four-legged: $2$ dogs and $3$ cats, so $5\times4=20$ legs. Goldfish have none. Total $18+20=38$.

**Answer: (C) 38**

ukmt-jk-2015-02.title: Use the middle number
ukmt-jk-2015-02.body:
The sum of five consecutive integers is $5$ times the middle one, so the middle integer is $2015\div5=403$. The smallest is $403-2=401$.

**Answer: (A) 401**

ukmt-jk-2015-03.title: Count the edges walked
ukmt-jk-2015-03.body:
From the diagram the ant's route consists of exactly five edges of the cube, each $18$ cm long. So it walks $5\times18=90$ cm.

**Answer: (E) 90 cm**

ukmt-jk-2015-04.title: Work from the last fraction
ukmt-jk-2015-04.body:
A day is $24$ hours, so $\frac18$ of a day is $3$ hours. $\frac16$ of $3$ hours is $30$ minutes $=1800$ seconds. $\frac14$ of $1800$ seconds is $450$ seconds.

**Answer: (C) 450**

ukmt-jk-2015-05.title: Estimate
ukmt-jk-2015-05.body:
$2015\times100=201\,500$, leaving $2015$ which is one more $2015$. So the quotient is $101$.

**Answer: (B) 101**

ukmt-jk-2015-06.title: Match the sides
ukmt-jk-2015-06.body:
Look at the left and right numbers. Rectangles A, E and C can be chained so that touching sides are equal: C (right $7$) next to A (left $7$), A (right $4$) next to E (left $4$). So C, A, E form the top row in positions I, II, III. Rectangles D (right $3$) and B (left $3$) form the bottom row, so D is in position IV and B in position V. The rectangle in position I sits above D, whose top number is $2$, so it must have $2$ on its bottom edge. That is rectangle C.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2015-07.title: Each cut adds 9 pieces
ukmt-jk-2015-07.body:
Cutting one piece into $10$ turns $1$ piece into $10$, which adds $9$ pieces. There are $4$ cuts in total, so there are $1+4\times9=37$ pieces.

**Answer: (C) 37**

ukmt-jk-2015-08.title: Find one-way times
ukmt-jk-2015-08.body:
Running one way takes $24\div2=12$ minutes. Walking one way plus running one way is $40$ minutes, so walking one way takes $40-12=28$ minutes. Walking both ways takes $2\times28=56$ minutes.

**Answer: (A) 56 minutes**

ukmt-jk-2015-08.title: Compare the trips
ukmt-jk-2015-08.body:
Walk-both-ways minus (walk + run) equals (walk + run) minus run-both-ways: the two differences are both $\text{walk}-\text{run}$. So walk-both $=2\times40-24=56$ minutes.

**Answer: (A) 56 minutes**

ukmt-jk-2015-09.title: Fill in from the bottom
ukmt-jk-2015-09.body:
Bottom row: $2,5,c,d,6$. In the row above, $7=2+5$ and $15=d+6$, so $d=9$. In the next row up, $27=(c+9)+15$, so $c+9=12$ and $c=3$. Now the row of four is $7,8,12,15$; the next row is $15,20,27$; the next is $35,47$; so $x=35+47=82$.

**Answer: (B) 82**

ukmt-jk-2015-10.title: Count squares and triangles
ukmt-jk-2015-10.body:
The staircase shape has $6$ squares of size $1\times1$ and $1$ square of size $2\times2$, so $S=7$. Triangles (half-squares and larger): four of size $1\times1$ halves, three of size $2\times2$ halves, two of size $3\times3$ halves and one of size $4\times4$ half, so $T=10$. Then $S\times T=70$.

**Answer: (D) 70**

ukmt-jk-2015-11.title: Count small triangles
ukmt-jk-2015-11.body:
Each of the first four horizontal rows of the shaded region has the same area as $5$ small triangles, and the fifth row has half of that, $2.5$ small triangles. So the shaded area equals $4\times5+2.5=22.5$ small triangles, i.e. $22.5\times4=90\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: (B) $90\text{ cm}^2$**

ukmt-jk-2015-11.title: Trapezium formula
ukmt-jk-2015-11.body:
Let a small triangle have base $b$ and height $h$, so $\frac12bh=4$ and $bh=8$. The shaded region is a trapezium with parallel sides $4b$ and $5b$ and height $\frac52h$. Its area is $\frac12(4b+5b)\times\frac52h=\frac{45}{4}bh=\frac{45}{4}\times8=90$.

**Answer: (B) $90\text{ cm}^2$**

ukmt-jk-2015-12.title: Bound the total
ukmt-jk-2015-12.body:
The sum is (two-digit number) + (two one-digit numbers). The largest possible is $99+9+9=117$, so the triangle is $1$ and the total is $111$. With the circle $9$ we get $99$ (and $89+9+9$... any other circle gives less than $111$ since $88+9+9=106<111$), so the two squares add up to $111-99=12$. Each square is $6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

ukmt-jk-2015-13.title: Make the others as small as possible
ukmt-jk-2015-13.body:
To make one integer as large as possible, the other nine must be as small as possible: $1,2,\dots,9$ with sum $45$. Then the largest is $100-45=55$.

**Answer: (A) 55**

ukmt-jk-2015-14.title: Count circle fractions
ukmt-jk-2015-14.body:
The shaded parts are the whole central circle plus a quarter of each of the four outer circles: $1+4\times\frac14=2$ circles. The unshaded parts are $4\times\frac34=3$ circles. The ratio is $2:3$.

**Answer: (D) $2:3$**

ukmt-jk-2015-15.title: Compare perimeters
ukmt-jk-2015-15.body:
Let the path have width $x$ m. Each side of the outer rectangle is $2x$ longer than the corresponding side of the garden, so the outer perimeter is $4\times 2x=8x$ longer. Then $8x=24$ and $x=3$.

**Answer: (C) 3 m**

ukmt-jk-2015-15.title: Corners
ukmt-jk-2015-15.body:
Each corner of the path adds $x$ to two sides, so the outer edge is longer by $2x$ at each of the $4$ corners: $8x=24$, $x=3$.

**Answer: (C) 3 m**

ukmt-jk-2015-16.title: Separate directions
ukmt-jk-2015-16.body:
The moves are $2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ m. Since it turns $90^\circ$ each time, the odd-numbered hours are in one line and the even-numbered hours in a perpendicular line. To be furthest away, all moves in each line should go the same way: $2+4+6+8=20$ m in one direction and $3+5+7=15$ m in the perpendicular one. The distance is $\sqrt{20^2+15^2}=\sqrt{625}=25$ m.

**Answer: (C) 25 m**

ukmt-jk-2015-17.title: Spend locks on containers
ukmt-jk-2015-17.body:
To open a box he must open the trunk, the chest it is in, and the box itself. Open the trunk ($1$ lock) and all $5$ chests ($5$ locks): that is $6$ locks, leaving $3$ locks for boxes. So he takes $3\times10=30$ coins at least.

**Answer: (B) 30**

ukmt-jk-2015-18.title: Write an expression
ukmt-jk-2015-18.body:
If he chooses $x$, the result is $2(4x-30)-10=8x-70$. This must be at most $99$: $8x\le169$, so $x\le21.1$. Largest integer: $21$ (giving $98$).

**Answer: (E) 21**

ukmt-jk-2015-18.title: Test the options
ukmt-jk-2015-18.body:
$x=21$: $4\times21-30=54$, $\times2=108$, $-10=98$, a two-digit number. The next integer $22$ gives $106$, three digits.

**Answer: (E) 21**

ukmt-jk-2015-19.title: Find when the poster is false
ukmt-jk-2015-19.body:
The cat changes activity at noon and at midnight. The poster is false exactly when the activity $2$ hours ago differs from the activity in $1$ hour, i.e. when a change occurs in the $3$-hour window between those two moments. For each change this happens for $3$ hours: from $1$ hour before the change until $2$ hours after it. With two changes a day the poster is false for $6$ hours, so it is true for $24-6=18$ hours.

**Answer: (D) 18**

ukmt-jk-2015-20.title: Count tiles in the 15th shape
ukmt-jk-2015-20.body:
The $n$th shape is a square with $2n-1$ tiles on each side. The 15th is $29\times29=841$ tiles. The colours alternate like a chessboard with black in the corners, so there is one more black tile than white: black $=\frac{841+1}{2}=421$.

**Answer: (B) 421**

ukmt-jk-2015-21.title: List the possibilities
ukmt-jk-2015-21.body:
If $\left(\frac bc\right)^2$ is a digit, then $\frac bc$ is a whole number (a rational square root of an integer is an integer). It is not $1$ as digits differ, and $4$ would give first digit $16$. So the ratio is $2$ or $3$. Ratio $2$: first digit $4$; $(b,c)=(2,1)$ or $(6,3)$ (the others repeat the digit $4$), giving $421$ and $463$. Ratio $3$: first digit $9$; $(b,c)=(3,1)$ or $(6,2)$ giving $931$ and $962$ ($(9,3)$ repeats $9$). The largest code is $962$, the smallest $421$, and the difference is $541$.

**Answer: (E) 541**

ukmt-jk-2015-22.title: Count cubes by layer
ukmt-jk-2015-22.body:
Each cube has volume $27\text{ cm}^3$. Both views show $4$ cubes in the bottom layer, so the bottom layer has at most $4\times4=16$ cubes; both views show $2$ cubes in the second layer, so at most $2\times2=4$ cubes there. The maximum is $20$ cubes, volume $20\times27=540\text{ cm}^3$.

**Answer: (D) 540**

ukmt-jk-2015-23.title: Squares have odd number of factors
ukmt-jk-2015-23.body:
Factors of a number pair up as $d$ and $n/d$, except when $d=n/d$, so the number of factors is odd exactly when $n$ is a perfect square. The three-digit squares are $10^2=100$ to $31^2=961$, which is $31-10+1=22$ numbers.

**Answer: (E) 22**

ukmt-jk-2015-24.title: Try Sally's seat
ukmt-jk-2015-24.body:
Number seats $1$ to $5$ from the left. Sally is in $2$, $3$ or $4$. If Sally is in $2$, then Dolly and Kelly cannot be in seats $1$ or $3$, so they must fill seats $4,5$, but Elly must be right of Dolly, and three people would need seats $4,5$: impossible. If Sally is in $3$, Dolly cannot be in $2,4$ or $1$, so Dolly is in $5$ and Elly cannot be to her right: impossible. So Sally is in seat $4$. Then Dolly and Kelly are not in seats $3,5$; Dolly is not in seat $1$, so Dolly is in $2$ and Kelly in $1$. Molly cannot be in seat $5$, so Molly is in $3$ and Elly in $5$. Check: Elly is right of Dolly. 

**Answer: (E) Elly**

ukmt-jk-2015-25.title: Use speed ratios
ukmt-jk-2015-25.body:
When Bridgit runs $100$ m, Carol runs $75$ m, so Carol runs $\frac34$ of Bridgit's distance. When Anna finishes, Bridgit has run $84$ m, so Carol has run $\frac34\times84=63$ m. She is $100-63=37$ m behind.

**Answer: (A) 37 m**
